title: Skim-run playbook + micro-sheet
body:
Purpose: tiny, fast-to-scan tracker for quick micro-bench runs — intended for iterative probing rather than formal bench reports. Use when I want a 15-30 minute sanity check on config changes (quant, cache, batch) and to record rough cost/latency tradeoffs.

Notes to self: keep columns compact; prefixed run ids so they sort by date (YYMMDD-#). When possible capture p50/p95 and a single cost estimate normalized to 1k tokens. Add link to run artifacts (logs/kernels) if a run looks interesting.

Quick table (comma-separated for easy copy/paste into sheets):
run_id, date, model, quant, batch, seq_len, tokens, p50_ms, p95_ms, throughput_rps, est_cost_per_1k, cache_mode, notes
240711-01, 2024-07-11, guanaco-33B, int8, 4, 512, 600, 42, 98, 35, $0.23, kv-prefetch, baseline after kernel tweaks
240711-02, 2024-07-11, guanaco-33B, int8, 8, 512, 1200, 48, 115, 60, $0.21, kv-prefetch, doubled batch -> slightly higher p95 (tail spikes)
240711-03, 2024-07-12, guanaco-33B, int8, 8, 1024, 2400, 85, 230, 28, $0.26, kv-disabled, larger seq increases mem churn
240718-01, 2024-07-18, mixtral-8x, q4_0, 16, 256, 400, 18, 40, 70, $0.10, kv-prefetch, good perf, lower quality TODO verify tokens-per-second consistency
240725-01, 2024-07-25, mixtral-8x, q4_0, 8, 512, 900, 34, 82, 40, $0.12, kv-cache, test A/B with prefetching

Immediate takeaways:
- Prefetching KV cache usually drops p50 by ~10-20% for these models; effect on p95 inconsistent depending on concurrency.
- Increasing batch helps throughput but can add tail latency at spikes. Consider max-batch-time tuning.
- For long sequences the memory behavior is non-linear; watch swap and fragmentation on smaller instances.

Short checklist for next micro-run:
- [ ] Try max-batch-time=10ms for 8->16 batch change
- [ ] Capture kernel selector log (PR 432 changes)
- [ ] Run 3 warmup iterations before measuring
- [ ] Save flamegraph and nvtx markers if p95 > 2x p50

Questions / open hypotheses:
- Does prefetching help more for models with larger KV size (e.g., >20M keys)? quick hypothesis: yes but needs measurement with >1k tokens.
- Is q4_0 stable across sequence lengths beyond 2048? seeing artifacts at 1024 already for mixtral, need larger seq tests.

Scratch notes:
- If p95 keeps spiking, try route -> smaller model variant (cost tradeoff) or enable fallback to dedicated-1 for burst.
- Keep a copy of the coinflip prompt used for these runs: "Predict next token distribution for controlled seed" — ensures deterministic-ish token counts.

Minimal run naming convention: YYMMDD-##_model_quant_batch
Example: 240718-01_mixtral-q4_0_b16

Meta: this file is intentionally compact. If something looks promising, transplant into a proper bench doc under shared_drives/engineering/applied-ml with full-output capture and reproducible commandlines.

Raw commands (notes):
# warmup: ./bench --model guanaco-33B --quant int8 --batch 8 --seq 512 --warmup 3 --iters 20 --kv-prefetch
# perf capture: ./bench --dump-trace=trace-240711-02.json --nvtx

Links: quick run logs are uploaded to s3://redwood-bench/tmp/2407/ (look for file names matching run_id).

End of sheet.
summary: Personal micro-bench sheet for quick iteration: runs, p50/p95, cost estimates, notes and next steps. Lightweight, copyable CSV-style table plus action checklist.
